claims.title: Bayesian Boolean experiment value is concave in the declared model prior
claims.scope: finite Boolean hidden-model priors with fixed experiment subset and Bayesian K3 excess coding loss
assumptions: the same truth table and observation partition are used across priors
nonclaims: concavity does not assert the mixture prior is empirically justified

claims.title: Bayesian Boolean experiment value is sharply one-Lipschitz in prior total variation
claims.scope: finite priors on one common hidden-model support and one fixed observation subset
assumptions: loss is bounded in [0,1] before the K3 excess-cost reduction
nonclaims: the TV radius itself must come from a separate modeling or statistical argument

claims.title: Marginal Bayesian experiment gain is two-Lipschitz in prior total variation
claims.scope: differences of two Bayesian Boolean experiment values under a common prior perturbation
assumptions: both endpoint values obey the one-Lipschitz theorem
nonclaims: the factor two is a generic worst-case bound and may be loose for a specific experiment

claims.title: Strict nominal experiment-value and marginal-gain margins yield sufficient TV-robust ranking certificates
claims.scope: two-value or two-marginal-gain comparisons throughout one declared TV ball
assumptions: absolute-value margins exceed twice the TV radius for values or four times the radius for marginal gains
nonclaims: the sufficient margins are not necessary conditions

claims.title: The one-bit point-mass prior perturbation saturates the TV continuity constant
claims.scope: f(x)=x with no observation and priors (1,0) and (1-rho,rho) for rho<=1/2
assumptions: the same two hidden models are retained
nonclaims: not every finite problem attains the bound

claims.title: Bounded exact Bayesian prior-robustness audit
claims.scope: tight TV continuity, strict prior concavity, value/gain bands, ranking margins, and shifted-prior gain tests
assumptions: all priors and values use exact rational arithmetic
nonclaims: bounded tests do not generate a statistical confidence region
CI success is not evidence for simulation
